P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Restricted and sanctions-affected. From 8 December 2025 the Bank of Russia lifted its limits on outbound foreign-currency transfers for Russian citizens and non-residents from 'friendly' countries. Restrictions for non-residents from 'unfriendly' states continued to 7 June 2026. Western sanctions (US, EU, UK and others) cut many Russian banks from international payment networks, and most Western platforms do not serve Russia. This guide covers only lawful routes; it does not describe ways around sanctions.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest route for a freelancer: register as 'self-employed' (professional income tax, NPD) in the FNS mobile app 'Мой налог' ('My Tax'), which takes a few minutes. Alternatively, use a verified Gosuslugi (state services portal) account. Without registration you cannot use the regime or issue receipts. The self-employed do not file reports or buy a cash register; the app records income and calculates the tax (FNS). For income above the NPD limit (see L7), register as an individual entrepreneur (IP) with the FNS instead.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Since 2025, residents' main income is taxed on a five-band progressive scale: 13% up to 2.4 million roubles a year, 15% from 2.4 to 5 million, 18% from 5 to 20 million, 20% from 20 to 50 million and 22% above 50 million. Each rate applies only to the part above its threshold, so tax on the first 2.4 million is a fixed 312,000 roubles (FNS). Residence (183+ days in 12 months) and worldwide taxation of residents are the general rule (search summary, not captured). Many freelancers instead use the self-employed professional income tax (NPD); see L7. Sanctions sharply limit foreign platforms and payments (see W1).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: From 1 January 2026, the standard VAT rate is 22% (up from 20%; 10% still applies to essential goods) under Law 425-FZ. Simplified-regime (USN) businesses with 2025 income of 20 million roubles or more must pay VAT in 2026. They can choose 22% with input credit, or special rates of 5% (income 20–272.5 million roubles) or 7% (FNS). The threshold falls to 15 million roubles in 2027 and 10 million from 2028 (VATupdate). Sanctions limit foreign platforms and payments for Russian residents (see W1).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Professional income tax (NPD, the 'self-employed' regime): 4% on income from individuals and 6% on income from companies and individual entrepreneurs, up to 2.4 million roubles a year. Status is lost automatically above the limit. A one-off tax deduction of RUB 10,000 is applied automatically in the 'Moi nalog' app: 1% of income taxed at 4% and 2% of income taxed at 6%, giving effective rates of 3% and 4% until it is used up. Treatment of income from foreign clients and payment routing under sanctions were not captured.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money; major freelance and payment platforms exclude residents (sanctions or payment-partner restrictions). No clean workaround: these platforms exclude residents, for sanctions or payment-partner reasons depending on the country. Using someone else's account, a foreign address or a VPN to appear elsewhere breaches their terms, risks frozen funds, and can breach sanctions law. Do not do it. Legal options are limited to what local banks and licensed local channels allow (see P1/P2), and they change with sanctions policy, so check the current status before relying on any route.
